verified_findings.statement: Reduced hippocampal volume in MCI relative to cognitively normal controls was reported in three distinct cohorts using different structural-MRI pipelines (single-centre Nanjing, VBM/FSL-FIRST; Moscow Memory Clinic, FreeSurfer; ADNI amyloid-positive MCI, FreeSurfer/visual MTA/ASHS; the last conditioned on AD pathology). These studies do not establish hippocampal volume as the most consistently replicated structural marker: two also identified other structural measures as potentially informative or more sensitive in their analyses (cortical sulcal depth and gyrification; SRLM integrity and right dentate-gyrus volume, whose larger effect sizes were not formally tested).
verified_findings.notes: 6 papers (P-595 admitted, P-65/P-82 demoted 2026-08-22), 3 method families (VBM, FreeSurfer, radiomics), 3 dataset families (ADNI, Moscow, single-centre)
verified_findings.audit_note: AUDIT 2026-06-27 (per-VF head-to-head verification): 5/7 solid MTL-atrophy across 3 datasets; P-65 (hemispheric asymmetry) and P-82 (cortical morphometry) are structural-MRI but not MTL-specific - swap for cleaner MTL papers. | RESOLVED 2026-08-22 (source-PDF check): P-51 KEPT (paper's own VBM reports right-hippocampal atrophy pMCI-vs-sMCI), P-65/P-82 DEMOTED as recommended, P-595 admitted; 6 supporters final.

SCOPE: cross-sectional single-cohort continuum group-difference study, NOT a detection-accuracy replication (no AUC/classifier); MCI group is amyloid-stratified (MCI A+), not general clinical MCI. NOTE (relevant to IA-21): the paper's PRIMARY finding is that hippocampal-LAYER SRLM integrity is a MORE sensitive/earlier marker than gross hippocampal atrophy - hippocampal volume/MTA did NOT separate CU A+ from CU A-, whereas SRLM declined significantly already in CU A+. Not counted until operator G5.

verified_findings.statement: Across four studies that evaluated longitudinal or change information against baseline-only or less longitudinal approaches, incorporating repeated measurements or change scores was associated with improved discrimination. The evidence is not a clean test of a general longitudinal advantage: in the ADNI LSTM study the gain is not separable from the change of learner (a random forest given the same five time points did not outperform the single-time-point random forest); in two studies predictor measurements collected during follow-up overlap or are temporally aligned with the outcome window; one study (P-337) concerns progression from normal cognition to MCI or AD. Non-ADNI replication within this evidence set rests on one Swedish memory-clinic cohort.
verified_findings.notes: RE-DERIVED + non-ADNI-expanded. Direct longitudinal-vs-baseline comparisons. NON-ADNI (2): P-74 (NACC, trajectory classes improve), P-348 (Gothenburg MCI Study, longitudinal change-scores > baseline-only across 11 models). ADNI (3): P-168 (LSTM 5-timepoint vs RF index-baseline - cleanest), P-13 (survival, repeated measures), P-338 (follow-up provided most of the gain). CAVEAT: 3/5 ADNI; ADNI subset is survival-concentrated (P-13/P-338 both A8). 2 distinct non-ADNI replications (NACC + Gothenburg) = strong Tier 2; one more non-ADNI would reach Tier 1.

verified_findings.statement: Speech and language features (conversational transcripts, spontaneous-speech timing, conversational turn-taking timing) show MCI-versus-normal discriminative signal in several relatively small cohorts from limited recruitment settings (I-CONECT; the New York and Szeged memory clinics; Dublin): internally cross-validated AUC about 0.73 to 0.93 in the temporal-speech study and about 0.85 in the I-CONECT transcript study, and about 63% accuracy in Dublin. verified_findings.statement: Accessible, low-cost, non-imaging data streams (routine physical-examination and blood-test variables, dual-task gait, and a consumer EEG headband combined with tablet handwriting) show discriminative signal for MCI versus normal cognition in single-country cohorts. External validation is demonstrated for the routine-data and gait models, both within China. The handwriting-plus-EEG study reports very high within-cohort accuracy but has no external cohort; resting-state EEG yields about 70% accuracy for diagnosed MCI and only slightly above chance for preclinical cognitive decline; naturalistic-driving telemetry provides related evidence for an endpoint that combines MCI with dementia.
verified_findings.notes: RE-DERIVED (was 389, the worst over-aggregation). FOUR DISTINCT NON-ADNI datasets/modalities: P-2 (portable EEG MUSE headband); P-12 (CAUEEG, EEG deep learning); P-96 (CHARLS, routine physical-exam/blood screening, externally validated); P-69 (LongROAD, driving telemetry). Excellent dataset independence (all non-ADNI). Method families EEG-DL (A4) + traditional-ML (A1). Reinforces IA-NEW-12 (physical/blood-only screening) and VF-19.

verified_findings.statement: Efficiency-aware hybrid CNN-attention architectures can maintain high AD/MCI diagnostic performance with reduced computational cost (P-30, P-110, P-12); this addresses model-deployment efficiency, distinct from clinical-accessibility low-cost screening (P-76).
verified_findings.notes: Re-scoped to the actual compute-efficiency papers P-30 (factorized CNN) and P-110 (BrainViT). P-76 dropped from the claim: it is clinical-accessibility low-cost (non-invasive, no specialist equipment), NOT computational low-cost (FLOPs/memory/inference) - a different 'efficiency' concept; referenced in the statement only to mark the distinction. Third confirmation P-12 (Grillenberger 2026 Computers in Biology and Medicine) added 2026-09-09: 1D/2D self-attention models on CAUEEG (1379 recordings/1155 subjects) with ~18-21K parameters beat the 2D-VGG19 baseline (~20M params) by up to 4.1% accuracy with 16.8% higher specificity — explicit parameter-count efficiency evidence, and a NON-ADNI dataset family (CAUEEG) that upgrades dataset independence. Re-promoted to confirmed.
verified_findings.original_statement: Efficiency-aware hybrid CNN-attention architectures can maintain high AD/MCI diagnostic performance without heavyweight model cost
verified_findings.audit_note: AUDIT 2026-06-27 (per-VF head-to-head verification): MIXED: P-30,P-110 demonstrate efficiency/compute trade-off; P-76 low-cost is clinical/non-invasive not model-compute - mismatch. 2026-06-28 (human): re-based on P-30/P-110; P-76 removed from supporting_papers (conflates clinical vs computational efficiency); Tier 2. 2026-09-09 (operator): third independent confirmation verified (P-12, Grillenberger 2026, author-disjoint, explicit parameter-count efficiency on non-ADNI CAUEEG); re-promoted to confirmed (evidence_count 3).
verified_findings.demoted_at_audit_2026_09_14: Original supporter P-30 does not satisfy the statement's architecture construct 'hybrid CNN-attention': its block (summaries.md L16633-16696) is a pure factorised-CNN comparison - 'They compared 2D CNN, 3D CNN, and (2+1)D spatio-temporal CNN architectures'; Key methods '2D CNN, 3D CNN, (2+1)D convolutional architecture, augmentation, cross-validation' - with no attention mechanism anywhere, and its efficiency evidence is training convergence speed ('It converged nearly 2x faster than standard 3D CNN'), not parameter/FLOP/inference cost. The record's own notes already concede 'P-30 (factorized CNN)'. Only P-110 (BrainViT, 'hybrid multiscale convolution-attention model', L2868-2941) and P-12 (1D/2D self-attention EEG models, L13327-13409) satisfy the wording, so the 3-confirmation minimum for the statement AS WRITTEN is not met and the statement misdescribes a supporter it cites by ID. Demoted from confirmed to pending_human_review at the 2026-09-14 audit (findings_VF.json VF-17, major).
verified_findings.audit_note_2026_09_14: 2026-09-14 audit (not a gate action). (1) status confirmed -> pending_human_review; gate_verified false; supporting_papers left unchanged at [P-30, P-110, P-12]. The NEW supporter P-12 fits: block L13327-13409 '1D and 2D Convolutional Neural Networks with self-attention mechanisms', 'Attention models used significantly fewer parameters (~18K-21K vs. ~20M for baseline)', 'Both outperformed the 2D-VGG19 baseline (60.60%-65.98%) with up to 4.1% higher test accuracy, 16.8% higher specificity'. P-110 fits: 'hybrid multiscale convolution-attention model', 'fewer parameters and reduced computational cost versus heavier baselines' (sample size 'Not reported in source'). The ORIGINAL supporter P-30 is a (2+1)D factorised CNN with no attention component and convergence-speed efficiency evidence. OPERATOR OPTIONS: (i) re-word the statement to 'efficiency-oriented deep architectures (factorised CNN, CNN-attention hybrids) maintain or improve AD/MCI diagnostic performance at reduced computational cost', under which all three supporters fit and the re-promotion can stand; or (ii) keep the hybrid CNN-attention wording and hold at 2 (P-110, P-12) pending a third hybrid paper. Secondary caveats for the operator: P-12's parameter saving is reported as an outcome not a design goal ('efficiency-aware' is a stretch) and its absolute accuracy is 70.11% (EEG MCI-vs-HC), which strains 'maintain high ... diagnostic performance' even though it beats its baseline. (2) Independence fields CONFIRMED and left unchanged: registry Dataset P-30=ADNI, P-110=ADNI, P-12=CAUEEG (ADNI_Dependent=false) = 2 dataset families, independence_met true is accurate. (3) statement parenthetical updated from '(P-30, P-110)' to '(P-30, P-110, P-12)' so it matches supporting_papers/evidence_count=3; bookkeeping alignment only. (4) triage_note_2026_09_09 ('demoted to insufficient_support ... held pending a third independent confirmation') is HISTORICAL: it predates the 2026-09-09 re-promotion recorded in notes/audit_note and the present 2026-09-14 demotion; retained verbatim, not deleted.

verified_findings.statement: In Chinese community, occupational and clinical cohorts, education and psychosocial/functional factors (education, social engagement or support, loneliness, depression/anxiety, functional disability) rank among the leading predictors of MCI risk in interpretable (SHAP) models that entered no laboratory measures.
verified_findings.notes: Four DISTINCT non-ADNI Chinese population cohorts (occupational N=1938, community survey N=6434, depression N=1964, chronic-pain N=612); 3 method families (XGBoost/LightGBM/RF); total N=10948. Properly independence-checked (unlike over-aggregated VF-02/03/05/06/12/16). STRUCTURAL LIMITATION: all Chinese cohorts - do NOT generalize to Western/global populations (education/social structures differ). Awaiting replication in Western/African/South American cohorts before generalization. Cross-cultural partial corroboration: IA-NEW-10 (P-266, Pune India) also found education significant. Confirms cognitive-reserve / social-determinant theory; in screening even sociodemographic vars dominate biological ones.

verified_findings.notes: Independent method families (6): P-518 (rs-fMRI ROI connectivity, Australian local - fronto-temporal decoupling separates mdaMCI where hippocampal subvolume AND cortical thickness do not); P-478 (MR elastography, Delaware - low DG-CA3 stiffness predicts aMCI regardless of volume, B=-0.11 p<0.001; combined stiffness+volume AUC 0.85 vs stiffness-alone 0.71 / volume-alone 0.77); P-432 (quantitative T2 relaxometry, Bristol UK - MTL T2 heterogeneity predicts memory decline where absolute T2 did not); P-460 (meta-analysis of 50 studies - whole-brain volume NOT significantly reduced in either aMCI g=-0.22 p=0.095 or naMCI g=-0.17 p=0.24); P-584 (multimodal Cox, PREVENT-AD - hippocampal volume non-predictive for CU-to-MCI; MEG alpha short-term and neocortical amyloid long-term carry the signal); P-581 (cortical minicolumn diffusivity, NACC N=826 - outperforms hippocampal/cortical volume and thickness in survival). Datasets (6): AU local, Delaware, Bristol UK, 50-study synthesis, PREVENT-AD, NACC. SCOPE CAVEAT: qualifies rather than negates volumetric markers - hippocampal volume retains value at the MCI-to-AD stage (P-587) and for AD-vs-control contrasts; the claim is about EARLINESS and sole-sufficiency. Adversarially source-verified; grounding_ok=true.

verified_findings.statement: Adding expensive molecular modalities (amyloid/FDG-PET, CSF) on top of structural MRI or neurocognitive testing yields only modest-to-negligible incremental PROGNOSTIC value for MCI-to-AD conversion in several comparisons - a scope boundary on the general multimodal-superiority finding (VF-02).
verified_findings.notes: Retained after adversarial verification (P-503 DROPPED: adds only structural-MRI trajectory to cognition, no molecular modality, and shows a LARGE gain F1 60->77% - contradicts the theme; P-436 DROPPED: MRI-vs-neuropsychology diagnosis, no molecular modality). P-532 (radiomic Cox, ADNI + external Huashan - within-study head-to-head: dual-modality PET+MRI only modestly beats single-modality, C-index 0.798); P-507 (MLP, ADNI - MRI-only matches/exceeds prior methods that added PET/CSF/cognition, ~80% acc; vs-literature not within-study); P-493 (narrative review - neurocognitive assessment >= biomarkers for conversion at lower cost). WEAK-INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT: only P-532 is a within-study head-to-head; P-532 and P-507 are both ADNI-centric (partial dataset overlap) and P-493 is a review - so this is a Tier3 caveat/scope finding, NOT a strong consensus. RECONCILIATION with VF-02: VF-02's gains came from adding FUNCTIONAL to structural or in DETECTION; adding PET/CSF to already-strong structural/cognitive data for PROGNOSIS shows diminishing returns.

verified_findings.statement: EEG/MEG connectivity, graph/network and complexity measures discriminate MCI from controls in six independent single-site studies, mostly by group tests or classifiers with optimistic validation, and may reveal alterations that spectral band power misses (one study shows this under matched correction; three show it only in part). The corpus does not establish that these measures outperform spectral band power: the four within-study comparisons that report a discrimination metric find spectral or power-bearing features ahead or about even, none tested. Nor does it show that multi-domain combinations discriminate MCI best: the one test found a spectral-plus-connectivity combination worse than spectral power alone for MCI.
verified_findings.notes: Retained after adversarial verification (P-447 DROPPED: PD-MCI-specific population mismatch, and its claim is coupling-beats-either-single-feature, not network-beats-spectral). P-553 (19-ch rsEEG, Korea - spectral power does NOT distinguish MCI from HC, but wPLI connectivity / graph efficiency / complexity do); P-501 (rsEEG, Michigan Black-American cohort - multiscale connectivity ensemble >91% acc, static single-window inadequate); P-463 (source MEG, Japan - frequency-dependent connectivity-structure metrics differentiate HC-MCI, with DoD-SD significant for all three group pairs); P-480 (rsEEG microstates, Florence - temporal-dynamics degradation, not topography, differentiates MCI). 4 distinct method families, 4 distinct datasets. CAVEAT: all single/two-site - ties to open gap ACTOR-G-013 on EEG/MEG cross-site validation.

verified_findings.statement: Across three studies, finer-grained structural descriptors provided evidence of greater prognostic or model-based importance than conventional whole-structure measures: hippocampal surface morphometry outperformed hippocampal-volume baselines for predicting progression to amnestic MCI in cognitively unimpaired adults (Arizona and ADNI); cortical minicolumn diffusivity provided stronger prognostic separation than cortical volume fraction for MCI-to-dementia progression in NACC (numerically but not significantly stronger than hippocampal volume); and cortical grey-matter fractal dimension was the highest-ranked MRI feature by SHAP importance in vascular MCI (VMCI-Tuscany). These are not equivalent measures of superiority (classification accuracy, survival separation, SHAP importance). No equally clean head-to-head of hippocampal subfield volume against whole-hippocampal volume was identified; sulcal-width and tract-segment findings provide related but methodologically different comparisons.
verified_findings.notes: Cross-era, within structural-MRI, diverse descriptors: P-177 (hippocampal SURFACE multivariate morphometry ~92% vs volume 79% Arizona / 72% ADNI); P-245 (cortical FRACTAL dimension best MRI feature, XGBoost AUC 0.69, VMCI-Tuscany N=64); P-560 (SULCAL width AUC 0.907 outperforms cortical thickness in every contrast, Bologna); P-581 (cortical MINICOLUMN diffusivity beats hippocampal+cortical volume+thickness in KM survival, NACC N=826); P-408 (splenium SUB-TRACTS AUC 0.75 beat whole-splenium, NACC); P-91 (tract-SEGMENT, right-IFOF anterior AUC 0.80 beats whole-tract averaging, PD-local). PARTIAL: P-182 (hippocampal SUBFIELDS unevenly informative, whole-volume ~10.5% redundant, ADNI - attribution not head-to-head). DROPPED after verification: P-45 (callosal shape - CSF-correlation only, no performance-vs-volume), P-198 (comparator was a no-covariate baseline; cortical thickness AUC 0.78 actually beat sulcal width 0.71), P-183 (texture-vs-NEUROPSYCH, not vs volume). Independence: >=5 truly distinct datasets (Arizona, VMCI-Tuscany, Bologna, NACC, PD-local; +ADNI partial) - P-408 & P-581 share NACC. SCOPE: within-structural-MRI granularity claim; does NOT contradict VF-01 (MTL atrophy most REPLICATED != best-performing). Generalises IA-38 (P-560) and IA-37 (P-581). | EXTENDED 2026-08-26 (P-898..907 batch): P-899 (CBR-TLSA Bangalore, India; 36 HC + 27 MCI; FreeSurfer subfield volumetry) adds a 7th independent dataset family (non-ADNI, South Asian) - MCI showed bilateral reductions in hippocampal tail, subiculum, CA1, CA3, molecular layer plus left presubiculum/parasubiculum/CA4/GC-ML-DG/HATA, with left presubiculum, parasubiculum and GC-ML-DG correlating with ACE-III memory in MCI (e.g. left presubiculum r=0.460, p=0.024).

verified_findings.statement: Loading the system reveals MCI where the unloaded counterpart does not: within the same study, the same measure taken under a harder condition (dual-task or curved-path walking, peripheral-attention reaction time) separates MCI from cognitively healthy controls while under the simpler condition it does not. Microstructural-against-volume dissociations hold only in part in this corpus.
verified_findings.notes: Each member runs its OWN comparison between the sensitive and the insensitive measure in the same participants. P-651 (multi-shell NODDI of FreeSurfer hippocampal subfields, Chongqing CSVD cohort, N=169): comparing CSVD-MCI directly with CSVD-without-cognitive-impairment, hippocampal VOLUME did not differ significantly while left CA1-3 FISO and NDI did. P-666 (64-direction DTI with TBSS plus atlas ROI, Wuhan metabolic-syndrome cohort, N=104): between MetS-MCI and MetS-NC, whole-brain skeleton analysis found 6.02% of voxels with raised MD and 4.38% with raised lambda23 but reported no FA difference for that contrast, and the lambda23 extent relative to the same healthy controls was roughly eightfold larger in the MCI arm (34.84%) than the cognitively normal arm (4.56%) while lambda1 extent was comparable (59.95% vs 50.44%) - i.e. the myelin-linked parameter, not the axonal one, tracked cognitive status. P-665 (FreeSurfer surface morphometry plus Timed Up and Go, Guangzhou, N=60): single-task TUG did not differ (17.29 vs 17.60 s, t 0.47, p 0.64) while dual-task TUG (t 2.58, p 0.012) and dual-task cost (t 2.55, p 0.014) did, and on the imaging side cortical SURFACE AREA differed in left superior parietal cortex while cortical THICKNESS differed nowhere. P-661 (64-channel EEG event-related spectral perturbation, UT Dallas/Southwestern, N=35): early versus late amnestic MCI showed no behavioural separation at all (Go RT t 0.607 p .548; accuracy group effect F 0.12 p .730, with Bayes factors of 0.28 and 0.32 supporting the null) while central-cluster theta ERS separated them with d=1.155. P-662 (64-channel ERP reappraisal task, Shanghai Tongji, N=93): the valence difference score did not differ between aMCI and healthy elderly, while the arousal down-regulation difference did (t 3.205, p 0.002) and the late-window (1100-5000 ms) LPP difference did. Method families (5): NODDI multi-compartment diffusion; DTI/TBSS; surface morphometry plus instrumented gait; EEG time-frequency; task ERP with sLORETA. Dataset families (5): Chongqing CSVD, Wuhan MetS, Guangzhou, UT Dallas/Southwestern, Shanghai Tongji - all single-centre, none overlapping. SCOPE: this is a sensitivity claim about which measure detects a group difference, NOT a claim that the loaded measures have better diagnostic accuracy - no member reports an AUC (see ACTOR-G-021). It generalises VF-20 (volumetric atrophy is a late and insufficient marker) from neuroimaging into electrophysiology and behaviour, and it is the P-620+ era's counterpart to VF-24's within-structural-MRI granularity claim. [P938_P947: +P-940 - LASSI-L semantic-interference stress test: intrusion-error (PIE) load measure predicts aMCI-to-dementia (AUC 0.905) - a within-participant sensitive-vs-standard-measure design consistent with this VF.]
verified_findings.tier_rationale: 5 independent method families and 5 independent single-centre datasets, each supplying its own within-study head-to-head between the discriminating and the non-discriminating measure; no dataset overlap; no member is a review.
verified_findings.dropped_in_verification: P-667 considered and NOT included: its object-proportion measure failed to separate older adults from MCI while its ROC familiarity measure separated only young adults from MCI, so it does not supply a clean sensitive-versus-insensitive contrast at the MCI-versus-healthy-ageing level.

verified_findings.statement: Depressive symptoms or major depression and MCI are associated in three distinct samples using different designs: longitudinally in the US Health and Retirement Study (P-646), and cross-sectionally in a Chinese community sample (P-644) and in World Trade Center responders (P-656), where the association was not separable from substantial PTSD comorbidity. Temporal direction was tested longitudinally in only one study (P-646), which found associations in both directions at similar magnitude in two separately fitted models; these do not establish reciprocal causation or distinguish it from a shared common cause. The reviewed studies establish an association, but neither reciprocity nor a stronger evidential basis for the depression-to-MCI direction.
verified_findings.notes: P-646 (US Health and Retirement Study, Waves 4-14, 1998-2018, N=9317 and 9428, Fine-Gray competing-risks): baseline high-risk depressive symptoms predict incident MCI at fully adjusted SHR 1.20 (95% CI 1.08-1.34, p=0.001) and baseline MCI predicts subsequent high-risk depressive symptoms at SHR 1.16 (1.01-1.33, p=0.032). P-624 (Shandong chronic-heart-failure cohort, N=288, two-wave cross-lagged panel): T1 social frailty -> T2 MCI effect -0.578 and T1 MCI -> T2 social frailty effect -0.646, model fit RMSEA 0.068. P-644 (Tianjin/Shanghai community, N=1394, logistic regression plus bootstrap mediation): depressive symptoms independently associated with MCI at OR 1.82 (1.20-2.76, p=0.005), with significant mediation running in both directions. P-656 (FDNY World Trade Center responders, N=337, robust quasi-Poisson): major depressive episode adjusted RR 1.62 (1.16-2.27) and comorbid PTSD/MDE RR 2.31 (1.74-3.06) for prevalent MCI. P-657 (52-study meta-analysis, 29,321 older adults with MCI, 17 countries, 6 continents): pooled subthreshold-depression prevalence 28.1% (24.2-32.0), stable under leave-one-out and unchanged by trim-and-fill. Method families (5): competing-risks survival; cross-lagged structural model; bootstrap mediation; robust Poisson with population-attributable fractions; prevalence meta-analysis. Dataset families (5): HRS, Shandong CHF, Tianjin/Shanghai community, FDNY WTC, 52-study synthesis. SCOPE CAVEAT, which is the point of the record: the reciprocity half of the claim is design-limited. P-646's authors state that two separate models were fitted rather than one containing both pathways, so true bidirectionality cannot be fully established; P-644 is cross-sectional and its authors concede the two mediation directions cannot be arbitrated; P-624 has only two waves six months apart; P-656 is cross-sectional and states the temporal ordering is unresolved. Ties directly to open gap ACTOR-G-019. A SECOND caveat ties to ACTOR-G-018: every member dichotomises depression at a scale cut-off, so this is an association between MCI and a binary symptom flag, not a dose-response. [2026-08-26: +P-912 systematic review of psychiatric risk factors for MCI-to-AD progression (17 longitudinal papers; cross-species depression support) - 6th supporting paper, adds review-level design diversity.]
verified_findings.tier_rationale: 5 independent method and dataset families support the association at Tier-1 strength; the reciprocity component is downgraded because no member's design can license it, and the record is written so the two halves are separately citable.
verified_findings.dropped_in_verification: P-647 considered and NOT included: it found depressive symptoms (GDS) NOT predictive of 5-year conversion, so it is evidence about prognosis rather than about the association, and it belongs with VF-27.

verified_findings.statement: Whether depressive-symptom severity grades MCI neurobiology and prognosis is divided in this corpus: in four MCI cohorts, baseline severity scores did not track regional brain measures (one study) or conversion (three studies, each a univariate comparison with 17 to 28 converters), although in one of them major-depression groups had lower functional connectivity than subthreshold-depression groups; one study outside the supporter list finds a graded relation of severity to conversion (P-26), and another a univariate association that its authors' sensitivity analysis did not confirm (P-989).
verified_findings.notes: P-643 (VBM plus resting-state functional connectivity plus florbetaben amyloid PET, Korea University Guro, N=130): depression severity measured by K-GDS did not correlate significantly with ROI volumes or with functional connectivity in ANY of the four late-life-depression MCI subgroups, and the greatest FC reduction was found in the SUBTHRESHOLD-depression amyloid-positive group rather than the major-depression groups. P-647 (Shanghai Brain Health Cohort, N=1014 with 321 followed 5 years, Cox plus ROC): over five years only baseline MoCA predicted conversion (HR 0.738, 0.627-0.869; AUC 0.798), while GDS, ADL and every lipid marker were non-significant, and GDS's cross-sectional correlations with BDT and ADL were weak at |r| about 0.13. P-663 (FDG-PET plus informant-rated Interpersonal Reactivity Index, Florence, N=111): the Personal Distress regression model - the strongest in the paper at adjusted R-squared 0.379 - retained a NEGATIVE coefficient on diagnosis (B -3.785, beta -0.463, p=0.024) once Category Fluency and Rey-Osterrieth recall were entered, dissociating emotional contagion from cognitive stage, and the authors flag this as potentially contradicting the prior linear-increase account. P-662 (64-channel ERP reappraisal, Shanghai Tongji, N=93): HAMD and HAMA were statistically equivalent between aMCI and healthy elderly controls (5.28 vs 5.26, p 0.97; 7.87 vs 7.19, p 0.42), yet the aMCI group showed a significant reappraisal deficit (arousal down-regulation t 3.205, p 0.002) and a late-window LPP deficit - so the affective-regulation impairment is present at equal depression severity. Method families (4): multimodal MRI/PET group comparison; survival plus ROC in a community cohort; FDG-PET voxelwise regression; task ERP. Dataset families (4): Korea Guro, Shanghai Brain Health, Florence, Shanghai Tongji. SCOPE: this does not contradict VF-26 - depression STATUS is associated with MCI while depression SEVERITY does not grade the biology, which is exactly the pattern that motivates open gap ACTOR-G-018.
verified_findings.tier_rationale: 4 independent method and dataset families, each with a null or inverted severity relation established inside the study rather than cited; downgraded from Tier1 because three of four are single-centre clinic samples none of the supporters models severity continuously; P-26 (ADNI, N=397, adjusted HR 2.36 moderate and 3.79 high trajectory; linear restricted cubic spline on month-36 GDS) does, and finds a monotone relation, so the prognosis clause is divided rather than dissociated (rescoped by operator decision 2026-09-24, consistent with the 2026-09-22 rescope of ACTOR-G-018).
verified_findings.dropped_in_verification: P-645 considered and NOT included as an independent member: it is the same group and an overlapping Korea University Guro cohort as P-643 and would breach the independence rule. It is cited inside ACTOR-G-018 instead.

verification.scope: Grounded at finding-card level (summaries.md), NOT against source PDFs.

verified_findings.human_evaluation_note: CONFIRMED Tier 2. Four independent families. Excluding P-645 as same-group as P-643 is methodologically correct. Distinguishing depression STATUS from depression SEVERITY is a sophisticated move that strengthens both this and VF-26.

verified_findings.statement: Among physical-function measures, performance under load and functional capacity - gait speed, grip strength, dual-task cost - are associated with MCI where the corresponding static or mass-based measure is not.
verified_findings.notes: P-644 (Tianjin/Shanghai community cohort, N=1394, fully adjusted logistic regression, own within-study component comparison): sarcopenia OR 1.67 (1.04-2.68, p=0.033), handgrip strength OR 0.97 (0.94-0.99, p=0.006) and gait speed OR 0.16 (0.07-0.35, p<0.001) were each associated with MCI, whereas the skeletal muscle index - the mass component - was NOT (OR 0.86, 0.70-1.08, p=0.189). P-665 (Guangzhou, N=60, own within-study task comparison): single-task Timed Up and Go did not differ between MCI and controls (t 0.47, p 0.64) while dual-task TUG (t 2.58, p 0.012) and dual-task cost (t 2.55, p 0.014) did. P-637 (systematic review of 38 technology-aided motor-cognitive dual-task studies in MCI): identifies Dual-Task Cost as the key measure supporting stratification and risk prediction, while reporting that protocols remain un-standardised and no pooled accuracy exists. Method families (3): fully adjusted logistic regression with component decomposition; instrumented single-versus-dual-task timing with surface morphometry; systematic review. Dataset families (3): Tianjin/Shanghai community, Guangzhou clinic/community, 38-study synthesis. SCOPE: the underlying principle is the same as VF-25 and VF-20 - load reveals what the static measure misses - but it is stated separately here because the modality (motor/physical function) and the comparison (mass versus performance) are distinct.
verified_findings.tier_rationale: Only 3 members, one of which is a review with no pooled estimate, and both primary members are cross-sectional Chinese cohorts - so dataset diversity is narrow. Recorded as supporting evidence for the VF-20/VF-25 family rather than as an independent strong consensus; a non-Chinese primary replication would lift it to Tier2.
verified_findings.dropped_in_verification: P-639 considered and NOT included: its walking-device/assistance variable is a covariate that differed between event and non-event groups, not a within-study contrast against a static measure.

verified_findings.statement: How MCI status and its correlates are ascertained is a first-order determinant of the reported estimate, not a second-order nuisance: within the same condition, the measurement source and the case definition move prevalence estimates by a factor of two or more, and this dominates every substantive moderator tested alongside it.
verified_findings.notes: P-654 (52-study sleep-disturbance meta-analysis in MCI, 25,915 participants, 24 countries): measurement method is the largest single moderator - self-reported 49.4% (40.4-58.4) versus informant-rated 23.7% (20.6-26.7) versus clinician-administered 33.8% (24.3-43.2), df=2, Q=30.173, p<0.001 - and research design also separates (cross-sectional 40.8% versus cohort 26.6%, Q=12.565, p<0.001) while sample source does not (population 33.5% versus clinic 38.0%, p=0.395). P-657 (52-study subthreshold-depression meta-analysis in MCI, 29,321 participants, 17 countries): ascertainment method separates (DSM-based 21.3% versus 28.9% in studies that identified depressive symptoms without a clinical assessment excluding MDD; exploratory, and the authors say the subgroup differences should not be read as definitive) as does referral setting (hospital 36.2% versus community 21.6%), against a pooled estimate of 28.1%. P-648 and P-650 (both UK Biobank, ICD-10 and registry-linked ascertainment) accrue incident MCI at 1.4% over a median 13.0 years and 1.6% over a mean 13.1 years respectively - orders of magnitude below the 17.3% to 65.2% cross-sectional prevalences reported by cognitively-ascertained cohorts in the same batch (P-644 17.3%, P-656 45.4%, P-639 65.2%). These are cumulative incidences, not prevalences, so the contrast is not like for like; neither paper compares its rate with other cohorts, and only P-648 comments on it, noting that health-conscious UK Biobank volunteers may have led incidence to be underestimated. INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT, stated up front: P-648 and P-650 share the UK Biobank dataset and count as ONE dataset family, and P-654 and P-657 are both prevalence meta-analyses and count as ONE method family with a second dataset family, giving 3 method and 3 dataset families rather than 4. Ties directly to open gap ACTOR-G-017 (nobody has applied two definitions to one cohort) and to ACTOR-G-016 (nobody has measured source discordance within-subject). EXTENSION 2026-08-26 (batch P-918..P-927): reliable-change measurement method is itself an ascertainment determinant - P-924 (Utah RBANS-SRB) shows traditional baseline-vs-followup comparisons reveal little change while SRB z-scores reveal significant below-expected decline; P-926 (Vienna NTBV-RCI) shows RCI detects stage-dependent deterioration (SCD<MCI<AD converters). Both independently demonstrate that HOW change is scored determines the reported estimate. [P928_P937: +P-937 - five-dataset criteria-driven progression heterogeneity 10% vs >30% at 4 years]. [P948_P957: +P-955 (consensus 44% vs actuarial 53% vs LCA 41% in the same N=354 sample; method-dependent racial difference in classification (no formal interaction test)) - direct within-sample demonstration that method choice moves the estimate.] [P958_P967: +P-962 (Aberdeen 1921/1936 Scottish birth cohorts with childhood IQ at ~11y) - test-score-only MCI criteria (1.5 SD below mean) lack TEMPORAL stability and IQ-discrepancy adjustment does not rescue prediction, i.e. the case-definition itself determines whether 'MCI' is a stable class; direct support for the ascertainment-determinant thesis.] [P968_P977: +P-971 - ADNI N=329: practice-effect (PE) adjustment is itself an ascertainment determinant - adjusting for PEs raised the number classified as MCI at the 1-year follow-up by 9.2% (272 vs 249), cut apparent reversion 28.8% (57 vs 80), raised single-domain stability 12.0%, and DOUBLED incident-dementia HR; 72.2% of PE-unadjusted 'false reverters' were amyloid/tau positive.] [P978_P987: +P-982 - Thai metabolic-risk clinic: MoCA<25-only ascertainment yields 82.7% "MCI" prevalence (348/421), versus 19.8% consensus-Petersen prevalence in P-981 community cohort - a >4x ascertainment-driven prevalence gap in the same task class, the largest measurement-source effect recorded in this finding.]
verified_findings.extension_2026_09_04_miner: Mined 2026-09-04 from batch P-1046 (PENDING HUMAN G4, rule 0 - not gate-verified): +P-1046 as supporter. Evidence: 100% US Medicare FFS+Advantage 2015-2019 observed/expected analysis - only 6.2-7.9% of expected MCI cases diagnosed (92% undiagnosed); detection 0.039 Black / 0.048 Hispanic vs 0.098 non-Hispanic White (minority detection less than half the majority rate) - the largest single ascertainment effect recorded in this finding. Caveat kept: ICD-coded detection may undercount in groups with documented access barriers (author-stated).

verified_findings.statement: Across three intervention classes (non-invasive brain stimulation, multicomponent exercise, computerised cognitive training), meta-analyses report positive pooled effects on selected cognitive outcomes, some in the moderate-to-large range (roughly SMD or Hedges g 0.8 to 1.5), but the effects are heterogeneous across domains, interventions and populations (multicomponent exercise g 0.98 for global cognition but 0.45 for executive function; computerised training in mixed MCI and dementia samples). They often rest on modest trial numbers and small individual trials, heterogeneity is substantial where reported (I2 about 63 to 93% in MCI and mixed pools), different instruments are standardised as SMDs, and the brain-stimulation syntheses share trials, so no harmonised MCI effect size emerges. The largest magnitudes (g 4.3 to 5.6) come from two-study pools in non-MCI dementia samples; the same synthesis reports a small short-term rTMS effect (g = 0.40) in mixed MCI and dementia samples, stable across sensitivity and leave-one-out analyses.

verified_findings.dataset_families: distinct trial corpora per meta-analysis (all non-ADNI)
verified_findings.notes: NIBS: P-373 reports 'sustained' tDCS effects of g=4.28 (cognitive flexibility) and g=5.60 (visuospatial) - larger than any approved cognitive drug; P-461 (19 RCTs, 599 pts) SMD 1.52 [0.49-2.56] with 'possible inadequate blinding'; P-520 (12 RCTs, 329) SMD 0.83, I^2=65-71%; P-427 (25 RCTs) SMDs 0.80/0.85/-0.96 with substantial heterogeneity and a harmonised-endpoint call. Exercise: P-603 (21 RCTs) global-cognition g=0.978 [0.298-1.659]. Cognitive training: P-655 (10 RCTs, per-trial N=19-117) SMD 1.21, self-described 'thin and fragile' (Egger non-significant, so framed as small-study/heterogeneity/non-harmonisation fragility, NOT proven publication bias). Nutrition: P-294 (41 RCTs) domain-specific effects with heterogeneity/publication-bias caveats. Each paper runs its OWN meta-analysis and independently reports the fragility - convergent independent evidence, not keyword aggregation. [2026-08-26: +P-914 non-pharm intervention review (heterogeneous protocols, short follow-ups, small trials) and +P-916 GABA/gamma review (human trials n=4-76, inconsistent biomarkers) - both corroborate the fragility thesis from review-level evidence.] EXTENSION 2026-08-26 (batch P-918..P-927): P-921 (CVSM immersive-VR cognitive training, uncontrolled pretest-posttest pilot, n=31) adds a 5th intervention instance - immersive virtual reality cognitive training - to the fragile-effects evidence: significant improvements on all cognitive measures (P<.001) in an uncontrolled design, consistent with VF-30's large-but-fragile thesis. [P928_P937: +P-929 - ChEI null regardless of amyloid = pharmacological class joins the no-credible-effect set]. [P968_P977: +P-968 (magic cognitive-training RCT n=24: MoCA + ERP P3 gains) and +P-972 (probiotic nutrition RCT n=130: VSRAD atrophy suppression, subscale-only cognitive gains) - both large-effect but small-sample/partial-signal, consistent with the pooled-fragility finding.] [P978_P987: +P-987 - TECH home tablet puzzle-gaming (n=38 pre-post, no control): MoCA d=0.52 and memory-recall p=0.006 are plausible but unadjusted for practice effects - reinforcing that no intervention class yet carries a stable, harmonised, controlled effect size.]
verified_findings.tier_rationale: 4 independent intervention families, distinct author teams, all non-ADNI; but this is a fragility/meta-evidence claim adjacent to the RETIRED VF-06 (small-N/ADNI meta-limitation). Distinguished from VF-06 by being a SPECIFIC, substantive claim about effect-size non-credibility (implausible SMDs + I^2 + non-harmonised scales), not a generic 'small samples exist'. Flagged for human adjudication of the VF-06 precedent.
verified_findings.fp_self_check: OVER-AGGREGATION: rejected - each is an independent within-domain synthesis reporting the same structural fragility with specific numbers. Generic-publication-bias: rejected - the non-generic core is implausible-magnitude + small-N + non-harmonisation making estimates non-credible at face value.
verified_findings.dedup_note: No existing VF concerns intervention (VF-01..24 are biomarker/imaging). Related to but far broader than ACTOR-G-009 (one undefined 'multi-ingredient' arm in one nutrition NMA).
verified_findings.human_evaluation_note: CONFIRMED Tier 2 (operator, 2026-08-01). Six independent meta-analyses across four intervention families, all grounding-spotchecked. Convergence is exceptional: NIBS (P-373 g=4.28-5.60), rTMS (P-461 SMD 1.52), exercise (P-603 g=0.978), cognitive training (P-655 SMD 1.21, self-described 'thin and fragile'), nutrition (P-294). Each reports the same structural fragility independently. Not a generic 'small samples exist' complaint - a specific claim about effect-size non-credibility driven by biologically implausible magnitudes, extreme I-squared, and non-harmonised scales pooled as SMDs. Correctly distinguishes itself from the retired VF-06 and flags that precedent explicitly. Tier 2 is appropriate: a meta-evidence claim about evidence quality, not a direct biomarker finding. CLINICAL IMPLICATION: no MCI intervention can claim a stable, credible effect size, and cross-intervention rankings (e.g. 'cognitive training beats exercise') rest on non-harmonised fragile evidence and should not guide clinical decisions. RENUMBERED from ACTOR-VF-25 to VF-30: the incoming id sits one character from the existing, unrelated VF-25 (load-reveals-what-static-misses) and all other verified findings use the plain VF-NN convention.

verification.fp_findings:
TRIPPED:
1. EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT (severe, x2). The headline clause "alpha is the only band that survives meta-analytic pooling across 12 independent M/EEG connectivity studies" rests solely on quote 8, an INTERPRETIVE ('Potential gaps or limitations') field. P-453's measured fields report only that alpha decreased; they are silent on other bands, so the exclusivity is an inference from silence. Aggravating: the miner's own FP self-check asserts "No significance/novelty field is used to establish a finding", which is contradicted by their own parenthetical on quote 8. Second count: "significantly LARGER" for the P-398 CKD-vs-CVMCI contrast has no significance language in any measured field.
2. UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS / EXCEPTION_ALREADY_IN_FIELD (fatal to the headline thesis). The proposed dissociation is that alpha is the aetiology-GENERAL component and delta/theta the aetiology-DISCRIMINATING one. Both cited papers' OWN Results fields show alpha-derived measures ALSO discriminating between MCI aetiologies: P-398 "CKDMCI-3&4 had the lowest parietal alpha power" (alpha separates MCI subgroups from each other, not just from HC); P-450 PD-MCI showed "lower alpha/theta ratio than AD-MCI and HC". The clean dichotomy is falsified inside the record's own evidence.
3. EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT (partial). P-453 is cited under the "regardless of the underlying disease" half, but it is a single-aetiology synthesis: it pools studies "along the healthy-aging to AD continuum" ('What did the authors do?') and its Significance field frames alpha desynchrony as "a candidate early neurophysiological biomarker of AD". Aetiology-contrast vocabulary never appears in P-453. It corroborates the alpha BAND across a second measurement family; it contributes nothing to aetio
verification.verifier_reason:
Verbatim quoting is clean — all 8 quotes match the source exactly — but field discipline is not, and the record's headline thesis fails on its own cited evidence.

Two independent defects hit the proposed statement as written. First, the clause "alpha is the only band that survives meta-analytic pooling" is sourced exclusively from P-453's '### Potential gaps or limitations' — an interpretive field that Hard Rule 0 forbids as evidence of measurement. The miner explicitly designates that field as the one establishing the claim while simultaneously certifying in their self-check that no such field was used, which is an internal contradiction that lowers trust in the rest of the self-check. P-453's measured fields report only that alpha decreased; the exclusivity is inference from silence.

Second, and decisive for the headline, the aetiology-general / aetiology-discriminating DISSOCIATION is contradicted by the miner's own quoted Results text in both power papers. P-398 reports "CKDMCI-3&4 had the lowest parietal alpha power" — alpha separating MCI subgroups from each other — and P-450 reports PD-MCI with "lower alpha/theta ratio than AD-MCI and HC". Alpha discriminates aetiology in both studies the record relies on, so the clean dichotomy cannot stand. Supporting problems: "delta/theta elevation" misattributes delta to P-450, whose measured fields report theta only (delta appears solely in the method's feature list); "significantly LARGER" is imported by the miner for the P-398 contrast, which carries no significance language; and P-453, an AD-continuum synthesis, is cited under the "regardless of underlying disease" half where its aetiology vocabulary is absent.

What survives full narrowing is the cross-aetiology alpha convergence: measured-field grounded in all three

source_reading_2026_09_28.narrowed_wording: At group level, MCI shows reduced resting upper-alpha activity relative to controls in two measurement families: lower high-frequency alpha (alpha2 and alpha3) spectral power in two small EEG studies (P-450, P-398) and weaker alpha-band inter-regional synchrony in a meta-analysis of 12 M/EEG studies (P-453, d about -0.25). verified_findings.statement_pre_2026_09_30:
VF (rescoped, group-level): REDUCED RESTING-STATE ALPHA IS A CROSS-AETIOLOGY MCI SIGNATURE IN THIS CORPUS, REPLICATED ACROSS TWO MEASUREMENT FAMILIES.

Supported core: every separately-reported MCI subgroup tested in the corpus's two resting-EEG spectral-power studies shows reduced alpha versus controls irrespective of underlying disease — AD-MCI and PD-MCI (P-450, Results: "Both AD-MCI and PD-MCI showed significantly lower alpha2 power and alpha2/alpha1 ratio than controls") and CKDMCI-3&4, CKDMCI-H and cerebrovascular MCI (P-398, Results: "All MCI groups showed reduced occipital alpha power versus controls"). The same band shows reduction in a second, independent measurement family — inter-regional synchrony — when pooled across 12 M/EEG connectivity studies (P-453, Results/Key findings: temporo-parietal d=-0.26, fronto-parietal d=-0.25). P-453's constituent cohorts sit on the healthy-ageing-to-AD continuum, so it corroborates the alpha BAND and the second measurement family only; it supplies no aetiology-general evidence. Three papers, three independent datasets (Trieste hd-EEG clinic cohort; national CKD/CV EEG archive; 12-study M/EEG meta-analysis).

DROPPED from the proposal (unsupported): the clause that alpha "is the only band that survives meta-analytic pooling" — that rests solely on P-453's '### Potential gaps or limitations' (interpretive) field; P-453's measured fields are silent on the non-alpha bands.

DROPPED from the proposal (falsified by the record's own citations): the alpha-is-general / delta-theta-is-discriminating DISSOCIATION. Alpha-derived measures also separated MCI aetiologies from each other in both studies — P-398, Results: "CKDMCI-3&4 had the lowest parietal alpha power"; P-450, Results: PD-MCI showed "lower alpha/theta ratio than AD-MCI and HC". Alpha is therefore not aetiology-blind, and no exclusive dissociation is claimed.

SECONDARY OBSERVATION — flagged for human follow-up, NOT established: in the two studies that contrast two MCI aetiologies inside one recording protocol, the non-AD arm carried the larger low-frequency excess (P-450, Results: PD-MCI "showed higher theta ... than AD-MCI and HC" — THETA ONLY; delta is an extracted feature but is never reported as a P-450 result. P-398, Results: "the CKD-related groups showed higher delta-theta power than both healthy controls and cerebrovascular MCI" — no significance statistic stated in source). These two contrasts are not commensurable: different non-AD aetiologies (PD, a synucleinopathy, vs CKD, metabolic/uraemic), different within-study comparators (AD-MCI vs cerebrovascular MCI), and different band definitions (theta vs a binned delta-theta). n=2 with incompatible comparators does not meet the convergence bar.

SCOPE CLAUSE: group-level effect only. No supporting study reports per-subject discrimination or AUC (all three record Best AUC "Not reported"), so this is NOT a claim that alpha reduction classifies individual patients and NOT a claim that band power outperforms network measures (cf. VF-23). Validation tiers are V2 (P-450 single-dataset group comparison; P-453 meta-analytic pooling) and V3 (P-398 retrospective observational subgroup analysis). P-450 N=36 total (15/11/10); P-453 = 12 studies; P-398 sample size is "Not reported in source". No block reports nominal or FDR-adjusted p-values, so the word "significant" is carried on the summariser's wording alone.

verified_findings.statement: MCI reversion to normal cognition is frequent (roughly 30-48% in community cohorts) and often durable across independent cohorts and designs
verified_findings.notes: Reversion is quantified by P-217 (6651-subject bidirectional transition model, Neurology), P-711 (48-study meta-analysis pooling 31% reversion), P-932 (LBC1936: 7% reversion, 12% progression), P-954 (WHICAP: 47.9% of incident MCI no longer meet criteria at follow-up), and P-957 (Nun Study: 30.3% reverted, 83.9% of reverters never developed dementia over 8.6y). At least one non-ADNI dataset in every supporter; methods span multistate Markov, meta-analysis, multinomial logistic, and Cox/Poisson. [P968_P977: +P-975 - Taipei memory clinic: first-year reversion 32.8% in EMCI vs 5% in LMCI, so the frequent-reversion finding is severity-stratified; EMCI reverters' dementia-free survival matched NCs, LMCI reverters did not.] [P978_P987: +P-986 - GAS/SNAC Sweden: reversion 43.4% (Petersen) vs 48.3% (stricter NP criteria) - the 30-48% population band is criterion-robust; single-domain impairment dominates reverter profiles (86.1%) and reverters retain lower dementia risk (HR 0.34/0.17), so reversion is real and favourable, not a definition artefact.] [P988_P997: +P-993 - BABRI (n=155) + ADNI (n=286) dual-cohort MRI covariance analysis predicts MCI development and reversion (AUC 0.692-0.809), adding an independent imaging confirmation of the frequent-reversion finding.] [P1128_P1137: +pending P-1133 (ADNI 2-yr reversion 18.17%, HR 0.104), P-1135 (ADNI multistate reversion 2-8%, post-reversion re-progression ~36%), P-1136 (criteria-consistent reversion context) - pending operator G4; ADNI-family supporters cannot count toward independence.]

verified_findings.band_inconsistency_operator_review_2026_: BAND INCONSISTENCY - flagged, not repaired (VF package item 5; handed off from the conflicts package). ALL THREE ELEMENTS VERIFIED AGAINST THE RECORD AND THE SUPPORTER BLOCKS. (1) HEADLINE: statement asserts reversion is 'frequent (roughly 30-48% in community cohorts)'. (2) THE RECORD'S OWN tier_rationale ASSERTS A DIFFERENT BAND: 'rates vary by setting (7-48%) so the claim is frequent-and-durable, not a fixed rate' - a 7% floor against the statement's 30%. The two cannot both be the record's band. (3) SUPPORTERS BELOW THE FLOOR, checked in their blocks: P-1127 (summaries.md L162815-162905, 89-study PRISMA meta-analysis, mean 5.2y follow-up, ADNI and etiology-predetermined cohorts excluded) reports 'reversion 8.7% (clinical) and 28.2% (population)'. The 8.7% is the CLINICAL stratum and so sits outside a community-scoped band - but its POPULATION figure, 28.2%, is inside the scope and BELOW the 30% floor, and it is the largest independent benchmark in the supporter set. The extension note that admitted it already concedes the point by arguing the 8.7% 'is the clinic-setting anchor of the band, not a contradiction' while saying nothing about the 28.2%. P-932 (summaries.md L141507-141632, Lothian Birth Cohort 1936, a population birth cohort with cohort-derived NIA-AA MCI and 'no clinical referral') is recorded in notes as 'LBC1936: 7% reversion, 12% progression'. THE 7% IS NOT A REVERSION RATE IN THE SENSE THE BAND USES. The block states 'Over the follow-up period, 74% (n=215) remained cognitively healthy, 12% (n=36) transitioned to MCI, 7% (n=21) reverted to healthy cognition, and 7% (n=20) maintained their baseline MCI status' - i.e. all four percentages share the whole two-wave sample (n=292) as denominator. Baseline-MCI participants are the reverters plus the stable-MCI group, 21 + 20 = 41, so reversion AMONG MCI CASES in P-932 is 21/41, about 51% - ABOVE the band, not below it. (That 51% is arithmetic on the block's own counts, not a figure the paper prints; the paper prints only the whole-cohort shares.) Every other supporter's figure is MCI-denominated: P-954 (WHICAP, L144265-144389) '47.9% no longer met MCI criteria' out of incident MCI cases; P-957 30.3% reverted; P-986 43.4%/48.3%; P-711 pools 31% overall and 36% for community studies. So the notes field puts a whole-cohort transition share in the same list as MCI-denominated reversion rates, and the tier_rationale's 7% floor is built on that mis-denominated number. (4) A FOURTH SCOPE LEAK, same defect class: P-975 (summaries.md L146905-147031) is a Taipei Veterans General Hospital MEMORY-CLINIC cohort - 'First-year reversion to normal cognition: 54 EMCI (32.8%) vs 16 LMCI (5%)' - so a 5% clinic figure also sits under a band the statement scopes to community cohorts. NET: the statement's 30-48% community band is contradicted from inside its own scope by P-1127's 28.2% population figure, is 'supported' at its low end only by a P-932 figure that is not an MCI-denominated reversion rate, and is contradicted outright by the record's own tier_rationale. The supporter set mixes community and clinic settings and mixes two denominators, which is exactly what a single headline band cannot carry. C-248 CONTEXT (why nothing arrived to fix this): C-248's 2026-09-09 human_defer_note endorsed a scope condition for VF-33 - 'restrict 30-48% band to multi-domain/criterion-based ascertainment; bar P-722 as supporter and refuter'. At the 2026-09-14 disposition that clause was WITHDRAWN, not merely declined: C-248's audit showed P-711's criterion stratification covers only 30 of its 48 pooled studies and that its largest contributor (Sha 2022, n=7422, about 23% of the pooled sample) ascertains MCI from MMSE alone, so the between-criterion spread is not a bound on the definitional family and the proposed clause would have excluded VF-33's own lead supporter's headline number. C-248 records the consequence explicitly: 'No scope condition is written onto VF-33 on this record's reasoning.' That disposal is sound on its own terms, but it means NOTHING was written onto VF-33 - so the internal band inconsistency above stands entirely unaddressed, and the only bookkeeping C-248 leaves is that P-722 stays in rejected_supporters. NOT REPAIRED HERE: the statement is unchanged, as instructed - choosing between narrowing the band, re-denominating P-932, splitting community from clinic, or dropping the parenthetical is an operator decision. RELATED STATE THE OPERATOR SHOULD SEE WHILE DECIDING: this record carries gate_verified=true with review_status='awaiting_human_gate' and manuscript_status='candidate_pending_g5', and selfcert_revert_2026_08_29 records that its earlier review_status was 'confirmed_claude_delegated_2026-08-26' - so the true flag sits on a record whose own fields say it has not been gated. Not changed by this pass.

verified_findings.statement: SCOPE BOUNDARY ON VF-13 / VF-18. Ocular MCI screening claims consistently outrun the discrimination evidence the studies themselves produce. Across five independent cohorts and four ocular measurement families, every frontier paper that proposes its ocular measure as an MCI screening instrument either (a) reports NO area under the curve at all (P-830 pooled no diagnostic accuracy of any kind across 126 studies; P-988 performed ROC analysis in a 40-month prospective conversion cohort but states no AUC), or (b) reports an internal-only AUC in the 0.84-0.87 band obtained on 74-86 participants at a single site (P-1163 AUC 0.841; P-952 AUC 0.87 by 10-fold cross-validation), with no externally validated ocular accuracy figure anywhere in the theme. In the single study that benchmarks the ocular channel against a brief cognitive screen inside the same cohort - the only such comparison in the theme - the ocular channel did not win: P-1006 reports demographics+eye-movements AUROC 0.752 against demographics+MMSE 0.767, a difference the study does not test, with 0.840 only from the combination. The replicated claims are therefore: ocular accuracy evidence is exclusively internal, and the one existing head-to-head went against the ocular channel. This bounds, and does not deny, VF-13 and VF-18.

verified_findings.residual_risk: The five supporters do not all make the same KIND of claim, and that is the strongest argument against the record. P-830 is a meta-analysis that never set out to fit a classifier, so its 'no AUC' is a property of its design rather than a failed screening claim; folding it in with three primary studies makes part of the pattern true by construction. More seriously, only ONE supporter (P-1006) actually measured the ocular-versus-screen comparison at 0.752 against 0.767, and a 0.015 AUROC gap on a single internal cohort is well inside noise - the other four establish absence of comparative evidence, not evidence of parity. A reviewer could therefore argue this is the generic small-sample/no-external-validation complaint already parked in VF-06, wearing an ocular costume, and that the honest record is a gap ('no externally validated ocular MCI marker has been benchmarked against a brief screen') rather than a verified finding.
verified_findings.dedup_note: Checked against VF-13 (retinal multi-modal imaging a viable low-burden direction; P-5, P-105), VF-18 (ocular channels repeatedly supported as scalable biomarker directions; P-5, P-105, P-109, P-952, P-966), VF-10 (consumer behavioural instruments reach high STANDALONE accuracy, with the note that none benchmarks head-to-head against a specialist instrument), VF-16 (low-cost screening channels viable without specialist imaging), VF-06 (generic corpus-wide small-sample/ADNI limitation, 0 supporters), VF-29 (ascertainment dominates estimates) and VF-30 (pooled intervention estimates fragile). VF-13 and VF-18 assert that the ocular direction is viable and scalable; this record states the accuracy boundary on that assertion, exactly as VF-22 states a boundary on VF-02, and shares one supporter (P-952) with VF-18 while making the opposite-signed claim about what its number licenses. It is not VF-10: VF-10 records the head-to-head as MISSING, whereas here P-1006 ran it and the ocular channel lost, which is a stronger and different statement. It is not VF-06, which has no direction, no effect range and no supporters. Gaps checked in T03_retina_eye_existing_gaps.md and existing_gaps.md: G-02 (no corpus paper uses retinal ERG as ML input), G-10 (no ocular study on the pMCI-vs-sMCI task), G-15 (no multi-vendor OCT validation), ACTOR-G-006 (no retinal-plus-central-neuroimaging fusion), ACTOR-G-060 (no longitudinal ocular-functional conversion study), ACTOR-G-068 (P-952 has no external validation). Each of those is one named absence in one sub-modality; none states the replicated cross-modality pattern that the accuracy which IS produced fails to exceed the incumbent screen and is estimated only in-sample.
fp_codes_cleared: CONCATENATION: not applicable - this is a VF, a single replicated pattern with a stated direction and a stated range (internal-only AUC 0.752-0.87 against a measured MMSE comparator of 0.767), not a string-join of two records.

OVERCLAIM_ARM (schema rule 2): P-1163, P-988 and P-1006 carry authors_overclaim flags, but the VF rests on none of the overclaimed quantities. From P-1163 it uses the reported AUC plus the design fact that the classes were fixed by the screener - which is what the overclaim flag documents, not what it inflates. From P-988 it uses the ABSENCE of an AUC. From P-1006 it uses the NEGATIVE result. In each case the record contradicts rather than inherits the overclaim. P-830's overclaim is its abstract's 'hold great potential'; the record quotes its Discussion verdict instead, as that paper's own digest instructs.

NON_INDEPENDENCE: P-966 was deliberately excluded - it draws on the same Korea Institute of Oriental Medicine / GARD cohort as P-1006 and shares authors (Julius Opwonya, Joong Il Kim, Jaeuk U. Kim, Kun Ho / Kunho Lee), so the two are ONE supporter; P-1006 is the one retained because it carries the head-to-head. P-933 was also excluded on review-includes-primary risk: it is a 2021 Frontiers retinal-biomarker paper and may fall inside P-830's 126 studies (search cut-off 15 January 2021). All five retained supporters postdate that cut-off (P-952 Neuropsychiatric Disease and Treatment 2021;17:3267-3281; P-988 2022; P-1006 2023; P-1163 2026) and come from five different countries and five different research groups.

verified_findings.original_claim_before_narrowing: SCOPE BOUNDARY ON VF-13 / VF-18. Ocular MCI screening claims consistently outrun the discrimination evidence the studies themselves produce. Across five independent cohorts and four ocular measurement families (pooled retinal structure/vasculature/electrophysiology, fundus photography, task-embedded oculomotor prognosis, saccadic classification, peripheral visual-field reaction time), every frontier paper that proposes its ocular measure as an MCI screening instrument either (a) reports NO area under the curve at all - P-830, a 126-study meta-analysis, pooled no diagnostic accuracy of any kind, and P-988 ran ROC analysis in a 40-month prospective conversion cohort but states no AUC - or (b) reports an internal-only AUC in the 0.84-0.87 band obtained on 74-86 participants at a single site (P-1163 AUC 0.841; P-952 AUC 0.87 by 10-fold cross-validation). In the ONE study that benchmarks the ocular channel against a brief cognitive screen inside the same cohort, the ocular channel does not win: P-1006 reports demographics+eye-movements AUROC 0.752 against demographics+MMSE 0.767, with 0.840 only from the combination. The replicated claim is therefore directional: the ocular MCI signal is real at group level but the accuracy actually produced by these studies neither exceeds the incumbent brief screen nor survives outside the sample it was estimated in. This bounds, and does not deny, VF-13 and VF-18.

verified_findings.residual_risk: The strongest objection is that this is a dressed-up tautology: MCI is by definition a milder condition than AD, so any marker graded by severity must separate AD better, and the record would then be recording arithmetic rather than a finding. Two supporters cut against that reading without eliminating it - P-1225 shows the analyte carries NO stage information once pathology is held constant, which a pure severity gradient would survive, and P-1202's MCI arm is a null (1 of 4) rather than an attenuated positive - but a reviewer could still argue that pathology burden and clinical stage are so tightly coupled that P-1225's adjustment is over-adjustment. A second, sharper objection sits inside supporter P-1231 itself: it reports P-tau217 at AUC 0.97-0.98, a single blood analyte far above the band this record describes, and its digest does not state which comparison that figure belongs to. No corpus paper measures p-tau217 at the MCI stage, so the 0.63-0.76 band may be a property of the analytes this corpus happens to contain (GST-alpha, RBP, cortisol, p-tau181, exosomal lncRNA) rather than of single fluid analytes as a class. The scope clause records this, but it is a real limit on how far the record generalises.

verified_findings.statement: For neuroinflammatory and microbial-inflammatory analytes, CSF and blood are not interchangeable compartments at the MCI stage. The corpus's systematic paired-compartment screen (P-1300: 63 inflammatory mediators, 485 paired CSF-plasma samples, validation subcohort, total n=1,360) quantifies the decoupling: only 6 of 63 mediators (CRP, IL1RAP, IL1RL1, IL6RA, PDGFRB, YKL-40) correlate robustly across compartments, and the one blood mediator that predicts MCI-to-dementia conversion (sIL6RA, HR 1.936 per SD) is drawn from that coupled minority. Consistent with this, the three corpus studies that measured the same analyte in both compartments in the same participants found the MCI signal in the CSF arm and not the blood arm - CSF-only LPS elevation at MCI (P-1233), a blood panel null where five CSF mediators separated MCI (P-1251), and CSF NGAL predicting 2-year conversion (OR 2.27, 1.15-4.46) with serum NGAL not predictive (P-1239) - but none of these three quantifies its blood-arm null, their serum and CSF assays are not analytically matched (P-1233 diluted serum 1000x against CSF 25x), so they corroborate the decoupling directionally without independently establishing it. Scope: neuroinflammatory and microbial-inflammatory analytes only; not a claim about plasma p-tau/Abeta assays, and not a claim that blood markers never work.

verified_findings.residual_risk: The three paired-null arms may be a POWER artefact rather than a compartment effect, and none of them quantifies the null. P-1251 reports no effect sizes, abundances or p-values at all in an n=68 cross-sectional sample; P-1233's serum stratum has 13 controls against 26 MCI and its ROC values were never printed numerically; P-1239 reports the serum result only as 'no significant association', with no OR, no confidence interval and no formal test of the serum-versus-CSF difference. Absence of significance in three small, statistically underpowered blood arms is not the same as demonstrated compartment dissociation, and the standard alternative explanation is analytical rather than biological - blood assays for centrally-derived proteins sit near their detection limits and are diluted by peripheral sources of the same analyte (P-1233 diluted serum 1000x against CSF 25x, so the two arms are not even measured at comparable analytical sensitivity). P-1300, the one supporter that is properly powered (n=1,360) and that formally tests cross-compartment correlation, is also the one that produces a blood marker that beats the CSF-adjusted model, which is why the claim has to be bounded to the uncoupled majority rather than asserted of blood generally. A human gate should ask whether a corpus paper exists that runs the paired comparison at adequate power and still finds the blood arm null.

verified_findings.original_claim_before_narrowing: Blood is not a surrogate for CSF at the MCI stage for NEUROINFLAMMATORY analytes. In every corpus study that measured the same neuroinflammatory analyte or panel in BOTH compartments in the SAME participants, the two compartments dissociate and the CSF arm carries the MCI signal while the paired blood arm is null: bacterial LPS is elevated in MCI CSF but not MCI serum versus controls (P-1233), systemic blood inflammatory markers do not differentiate MCI from cognitively normal while five CSF mediators do (P-1251), and CSF NGAL predicts 2-year MCI-to-AD conversion (OR 2.27, 95 percent CI 1.15-4.46) while serum NGAL is not predictive (P-1239). The one large systematic cross-compartment screen supplies the reason and the boundary: of 63 inflammatory mediators measured in 485 paired CSF-plasma samples, only 6 correlate robustly across compartments, and the single blood mediator that does predict conversion (sIL6RA, HR 1.936 per SD) is drawn from that coupled minority (P-1300). Direction: CSF-positive / blood-null in 3 of 3 paired designs; cross-compartment coupling ~6/63 (about 10 percent) of mediators. SCOPE: neuroinflammatory and microbial-inflammatory analytes only. This is NOT a claim about plasma p-tau or Abeta assays, and NOT a claim that blood markers never work - P-1300 shows one that does.

verified_findings.statement: CANDIDATE VF (status pending_human_review, gate_verified=false). Across three independent cohorts on three continents, structural-MRI measures fail to demonstrate a statistically distinguishable prognostic increment over concurrently measured cheap cognitive/clinical scores in MCI/SCD progression prediction - a consistent DIRECTION and an absence of demonstrated increment, not a pooled effect, with endpoint and metric heterogeneity that must stay inside the claim. P-1097 (Oslo, n=156) is the ONLY supporter that runs the adjusted head-to-head on the binary conversion endpoint: 'neither remained significantly associated with conversion after adjusting for MMSE-NR', while both volumes stayed associated with annual CDR-SB progression 'in both unadjusted and adjusted analyses' - the binary-vs-rate endpoint split therefore rests on P-1097 alone and is a single-cohort observation, not part of the verified finding. P-945 (ADNI, n=459) shows a null increment for discrimination-improvement only: IDI 0.090 (95% CI -0.062 to 0.170) contains zero, but NRI 0.246 (95% CI 0.021-0.848) excludes zero, so P-945 simultaneously demonstrates a reclassification increment and the record must not be stated as 'no prognostic value distinguishable from zero' unqualified. P-1073 (Mersin, n=190) contributes an UNCONDITIONAL null on a different endpoint: Fazekas grading and hippocampal atrophy 'did not significantly separate trajectories (p = 0.387/0.794; 0.116/0.094)' - cognition-defined slow/fast trajectory clusters in a cohort where 92.8% converted - in covariate models with demonstrated power (epilepsy coefficient 2.62, p = 0.002); it is not an adjusted test on binary conversion and must not be counted toward any binary-endpoint clause, and its visual-grading coarseness leaves its null consistent with measurement insensitivity. So narrowed: three cohorts converge that no structural-MRI increment over cheap cognitive measures has been demonstrated (a lost p-value under MMSE-NR adjustment, a zero-spanning IDI, an unconditional trajectory-separation null), suitable as the rescope/promotion evidence VF-05's demotion note asks for; the claim that redundancy is specific to the binary conversion endpoint is P-1097-only and stays a scope annotation pending further supporters; promotion additionally blocked until P-1060's Model 2 composition is read from source.

Its digest reports that MCI Model 3 - whose predictor list includes hippocampus volume alongside CSF markers - reached AUC 0.92 and was 'significantly above Model 2', but the digest never states Model 2's composition. If Model 2 is the cognitive-test model, then a fourth, larger ADNI analysis (n=796 MCI, 321 events) shows imaging-plus-CSF adding significantly over cognition, and the convergence claimed here is a selection of three studies that happened to land null. verified_findings.original_claim_before_narrowing: CANDIDATE VF (status pending_human_review, gate_verified=false). In MCI/SCD progression prediction, a structural-MRI marker adds no prognostic value distinguishable from zero once a concurrently measured cheap cognitive score is in the model, for the BINARY conversion endpoint. Three independent cohorts on three continents, using three different analytic frames, each run the head-to-head inside their own sample and each land on the same side: the imaging term loses significance under adjustment for the cognitive score (P-1097, Oslo, n=156: hippocampus and whole-brain volume both associated with conversion or not, but 'neither remained significantly associated with conversion after adjusting for MMSE-NR'); the incremental discrimination from adding three neuroimaging measurements to clinical change rates has a confidence interval containing zero (P-945, ADNI-1 + ADNI GO/2, n=459: IDI 0.090, 95% CI -0.062 to 0.170); and structural grading does not separate the cognition-defined progression trajectories at all in the same analysis where the cognitive tests are the most sensitive discriminators (P-1073, Mersin, n=190: Fazekas and hippocampal atrophy p = 0.387/0.794 and 0.116/0.094 against MMSE/GDS/calculation p < 0.0001). SCOPE CLAUSE (mandatory, and the part that gives the record teeth): the redundancy is ENDPOINT-SPECIFIC, not general. P-1097 is the one supporter that reports two endpoints under the same adjustment, and there the same two volumes remain associated with the CONTINUOUS annual CDR-SB progression rate 'in both unadjusted and adjusted analyses'. The claim is therefore about threshold-crossing (will this patient convert), not about rate of decline. SECOND SCOPE CLAUSE: the effect estimates are heterogeneous in kind (a lost p-value, a reclassification interval, and a set of null group-separation p-values), so the record establishes a consistent DIRECTION and the absence of a demonstrated increment, not a pooled effect size. P-945's companion NRI was 0.246 (95% CI 0.021-0.848), which does exclude zero, so 'no incremental value' is precise only for discrimination-improvement (IDI) and significance-under-adjustment, and must not be restated as 'imaging is useless'.

verified_findings.statement: SCOPE BOUNDARY ON VF-28. Within each cohort that measures it, the MCI group's mean walking speed is lower than that cohort's OWN cognitively unimpaired comparator by roughly 0.09 to 0.17 m/s, replicated in three independent cohorts: P-761 (Malmo, Sweden, instrumented walkway) 111 vs 120 cm/s, p < 0.001; P-695 (Sao Carlos, Brazil, stopwatch 10 m) 0.89 vs 1.06 m/s, group effect p = 0.001; P-682 (rural Shandong, China, interviewer-timed walk) 0.73 vs 0.83 m/s, p below 0.001. The ABSOLUTE values, however, do not transport across cohorts, and they invert twice: the Swedish MCI mean (1.11 m/s) is FASTER than the Brazilian cognitively preserved mean (1.06 m/s), and the Brazilian MCI mean (0.89 m/s) is FASTER than the rural Chinese non-MCI mean (0.83 m/s). The replicated quantity is therefore the within-cohort contrast, not any speed value. It follows that no fixed absolute gait-speed threshold can act as a cross-population MCI screening trigger: any cut-off placed to separate cases from controls in one of these three cohorts misclassifies the majority of at least one other cohort's group, in one direction or the other. SCOPE CLAUSES: (1) group-mean claim only - none of the three papers reports per-subject discrimination for gait speed, all three record no AUC, so this is not a claim about classifying individuals; (2) P-761's quantity is walkway STEP VELOCITY over six continuous laps, not a stopwatch usual-pace speed, and P-682's is an interviewer-administered timed walk, so the three absolute values are not measured identically; (3) the cohorts differ in setting (memory clinic vs community vs rural community), age composition and MCI case definition, so the cross-cohort spread mixes protocol, population and case definition - which does not weaken the operational conclusion that a fixed threshold transports across none of them, but forbids attributing the spread to population alone.

verified_findings.residual_risk: The strongest argument against is that the cross-cohort inversion may be entirely an artefact of measurement protocol and sample composition rather than a property of the populations, in which case the record documents a measurement-harmonisation problem and dresses it as a finding. GAITRite step velocity averaged over six continuous laps is not the same quantity as a stopwatch-timed 10 m usual-pace walk, and neither is the same as an interviewer-administered timed walk of unstated distance; instrumented walkways and continuous-lap protocols are known to yield faster values than single short stopwatch trials. The cohorts also differ in age (Brazilian MCI mean age 75.9 years against a rural Chinese MCI mean of 72.52) and in setting (memory clinic vs community), so the ordering of the absolute means is confounded several ways at once. The record's operational conclusion - that a fixed absolute threshold transports across none of these settings - survives that objection and is arguably strengthened by it, but the record's explanatory content does not: it establishes THAT a fixed cut-off cannot transport, not WHY, and a reader could reasonably demand that the claim be restated as a protocol-harmonisation gap rather than promoted as a verified finding.

verified_findings.statement: WITHIN a single MCI cohort, who counts as a case or a progressor is not invariant to the ascertainment readout, and the disagreement is large rather than marginal. Three independent trial and clinic cohorts each ran the comparison INSIDE their own data, on the same participants, so population and criteria differences are removed by design. (a) INSTRUMENT AND ANCHOR: applying the four instruments most used in MCI trials to the same ~605-609 patients at Month 12 classifies 27.3%-39.7% of them as minimal progressors and 2.0%-20.1% as moderate progressors - a ten-fold spread on the moderate criterion between MMSE (2.0%) and ADAS-Cog 13 (20.1%) - and two accepted change anchors applied to those same data give CDR-SB minimal-worsening thresholds differing about two-fold (MCI-CGIC 0.50-0.64 points vs GDS 1.00-1.08), with the MMSE failing the prespecified 0.30 anchor-responsiveness gate at every time point before Month 36 (P-865). (b) RATER: a blinded three-member expert committee and the examining site investigator, working from the same dossiers, agree only fairly on MCI due to AD - Cohen's kappa 0.327 with 71.0% overall agreement, falling to 40.5% on cases the investigator had diagnosed as MCI at two consecutive visits - and 42.7% of all endpoint events in the trial came from cases the investigator's own diagnosis did not support (P-866). (c) CHANGE METRIC: on the same two amnestic-MCI samples the conventional baseline-versus-follow-up comparison shows little change (and, where significant, improvement) while regression-based reliable-change scoring shows significant decline on all five RBANS Indexes and the Total Scale, ds |0.79-2.76| - the two readouts point in opposite directions (P-924). EFFECT RANGE across supporters: agreement in the fair band (kappa 0.327), classification-rate ratios of about 1.5x (minimal) to 10x (moderate) across instruments, threshold ratios of about 2x across anchors, and sign reversal between two change metrics. SCOPE CLAUSE: this is a within-sample non-invariance claim about individual case/progressor assignment. It is NOT a between-study estimate-variation claim, and it makes no claim about which readout is correct - none of the three supporters has a biomarker or pathological reference standard (P-866: 'AD neuropathologic biomarkers were not prospectively collected in the trial'), so the disagreement is documented, not adjudicated.
