verified_findings.residual_risk: The strongest argument against this record is that the three supporters do not replicate ONE finding but instantiate three different phenomena - inter-rater disagreement (P-866), instrument and anchor calibration divergence (P-865), and a change-metric specification difference (P-924) - so the unifying property may be an abstraction imposed by the miner rather than a convergence the literature contains. A reviewer who rejects the abstraction is left with three strong single-study observations and no verified finding. Two specific weaknesses feed that objection. First, P-924's traditional-versus-SRB contrast is partly DEFINITIONAL rather than empirical: the SRB expectation is constructed to include a practice-effect gain that the traditional comparison never models, so the two readouts are not competing estimates of one quantity and their 'opposite directions' are guaranteed by the formulas, not discovered. Second, P-866's kappa does not compare two opinions about the endpoint - the digest states plainly that 'Investigators did not offer endpoint opinions, so the paper compares committee decisions against what investigator diagnoses "supported", which is an inference the authors construct rather than a judgement the investigators made. The kappa statistics inherit that construction.' If that construction is unfair to the investigators, 0.327 understates real rater agreement and clause (b) weakens. A third, smaller risk: P-865's ten-fold moderate-criterion spread partly reflects the MMSE ceiling created by the trial's own MMSE >= 24 entry criterion, which is a design artefact of that trial rather than a general property of the instrument.

verified_findings.residual_risk: The strongest objection is that the pattern is fully explained by chance plus multiplicity, in which case the record's second half is an artefact rather than a finding. If the true effect of all four interventions is zero, the global null is simply correct and each 'positive' sub-score is one of many tested comparisons that reached p<0.05 - P-968 claims significance across four endpoint families from 12 per arm with no stated correction, P-972's positives are one subscale plus a baseline-conditioned subgroup, and P-1098 is single-arm with uncontrolled practice effects. Under that reading the convergence is a convergence of Type I error, and the claim that the narrower instruments are MORE SENSITIVE would be false. The record is therefore stated as endpoint-SELECTION, not as evidence that sub-scores detect real effects the global screen misses; anyone using it to argue for sub-score endpoints in trial design would be reversing what it supports. A second, weaker objection: three of the four supporters are Japanese memory clinics using the same instrument culture (MMSE-J/ADAS-Jcog), so instrument-specific ceiling behaviour in one measurement tradition is partly confounded with the cross-intervention replication.

This record is at the primary-trial level and names a direction (global primary null, narrower secondary positive, in the same participants). The prognostic null is evidenced only in P-991's brief-office-test arm; the two cross-sectional supporters support the discrimination ceiling only. verified_findings.statement: Elevated baseline blood-based p-tau217 predicts progression from MCI to dementia. Four independent cohorts on three continents/countries and three assay platforms all move in the same direction: AUC 0.876 for MCI-to-AD over a mean 56-month follow-up (Lleida memory clinic, Lumipulse, n=81 MCI with 45 progressors); AUC 0.88 for MCI-to-AD conversion over a mean 4.92 years (Malmo Memory Clinic, Janssen Simoa assay; 0.89 for the Lilly MSD assay in the same participants); OR 10.37 (3.00-35.02) for progression to dementia over ~3 years (1Florida ADRC, ALZPath Simoa, n=207 MCI followed); and HR 1.74 all-cause / 2.11 AD dementia per high-biomarker stratum in a population cohort (SNAC-K serum, 381 MCI at baseline, follow-up to 16 years). SCOPE: direction of association only. The AUC, OR and HR estimands are not commensurable, no cohort's cutoff transfers to another platform, and this is not a claim of superiority over NfL or GFAP (P-1421 ranks NfL at least equal; P-1423 selects GFAP first). STATUS: candidate / pending_human_review - the gate is the operator's.

verified_findings.statement: Amyloid-negative MCI is not a low-risk category, and within it the BINARY amyloid/AT call carries little prognostic information while CONTINUOUS sub-threshold measures grade the risk. Across three independent clinic cohorts on three continents: 36% of visually amyloid-PET-negative amnestic MCI converted to dementia within 36 months (Asan Medical Center, Seoul) and 40% of CSF A-T- MCI progressed in a real-world memory clinic (Milan); amyloid-negative MCI showed the SAME multidomain cognitive deficits and equally widespread white-matter compromise as amyloid-positive MCI (BABRI Beijing: lower FA in 14/20 tracts and higher MD in 16/20 in BOTH subgroups, the amyloid-specific increment confined to left hippocampal GMV). Within the threshold-negative group, continuous measures sitting BELOW the positivity cut separate converters from non-converters: regional florbetaben SUVR (left parietal AUC 0.762, P<0.001) and cortical diffusion AngleR (AUC 0.80, negative predictive value +21.25%).
verified_findings.required_design: any (two prognostic cohorts with >=32-month follow-up + one cross-sectional three-group comparison)
verified_findings.required_modality_family: C1 Neuroimaging (quantitative amyloid PET SUVR; diffusion MRI cortical microstructure; DTI + VBM) with CSF AT reference

evidence_quotes.quote: Converters showed higher regional SUVRs (temporal, parietal, precuneus, posterior cingulate, occipital); left parietal SUVR best predicted conversion (AUC 0.762, P<0.001); precuneus+parietal+composite model AUC 0.763; in ADNI, left precuneus SUVR highest (AUC 0.596, P=.006); conversion rate 36% at 36 months.

Among MCI A+T+ patients 90.91% converted to dementia (good PPV), while 40% of MCI A-T- progressed to a mix of AD and non-AD dementias (poor NPV). Adding whole-brain AngleR as an N marker gave good differentiation between stable and converting MCI A-T- patients (AUC 0.8) and substantially improved negative predictive value (+21.25%).

Both MCI subgroups showed similar multidomain deficits (episodic memory, attention, executive function) vs NC; only SCWT-C differed between subgroups. Both subgroups showed widespread WM compromise (lower FA in 14/20 tracts, higher MD in 16/20)

verifier_issues_not_carried_operator_rev: MECHANISM CONFLATION: 'continuous measures sitting BELOW the positivity cut separate converters from non-converters: regional florbetaben SUVR ... and cortical diffusion AngleR' merges two different things. AngleR is a diffusion-MRI cortical-microstructure NEURODEGENERATION (N) marker added on top of the AT call; it is not a continuous reading of the amyloid/AT axis below its positivity threshold. Only P-1350 supports 'the continuous version of the same thresholded biomarker grades risk within the negative stratum'. That clause therefore has ONE supporter, not two.

THIRD SUPPORTER SUPPORTS NEITHER OPERATIVE CLAUSE: P-1425 is cross-sectional (its own block: 'Cross-sectional design cannot establish progression') and is registry Task_Type T4 (association/mechanism) against T2 for the other two; its 21% amyloid-negative progression figure is cited from prior literature, not measured. It supports only a third, weaker proposition (amyloid-negative MCI shows AD-like deficits). The vf_new '>=3 genuinely independent supporters' test therefore passes only for a rescoped statement: the progression clause has 2 supporters, the continuous-grading clause has 1.

OVERSTATED P-1425 DETAIL: 'the amyloid-specific increment confined to left hippocampal GMV' is false. The block states 'Between-subgroup differences concentrated in the left hippocampal region: greater left-CH and FMAJ MD and left-HIP atrophy in Abetapos.' FMAJ (forceps major) MD is a white-matter difference outside the hippocampus, so the increment is not confined to GMV, and 'equally widespread white-matter compromise' overstates a result that did include between-subgroup WM MD differences. Similarly 'the SAME multidomain cognitive deficits' overstates the block's 'similar multidomain deficits ... only SCWT-C differed between subgroups'.

DESIGN FIELD MISSTATES FOLLOW-UP: required_design says 'two prognostic cohorts with >=32-month follow-up'. P-1386's follow-up is '32+/-18 months' - a mean with a large SD, so a substantial fraction of that cohort had far less than 32 months. The 'over ~3 years' in the direction field inherits the same inflation.

verified_findings.statement: MCI reversion to normal cognition is inversely graded by neurodegenerative / AD-pathology burden, and the factors that positively predict it are NON-neurodegenerative and largely treatable. Across three independent cohorts and two aetiologies: in PPMI, PD-MCI reverters were indistinguishable from cognitively normal PD on every CSF marker while non-reverters carried significantly greater p-tau/A-beta and t-tau/A-beta ratios; in the population-based SNAC-K cohort (2,148 participants, multistate Markov models, up to 16 years) elevated serum NfL and GFAP REDUCED the MCI-to-NC reversion intensity; and in a multicentre Italian community cohort the significant predictors of 1-year MCI reversion were biochemical and endocrine abnormalities (Na above ULN OR 7.3, TSH below LLN OR 3.6) while the neurodegeneration-linked variables (age, depressive mood, disease count, low WBC) predicted MCI-to-dementia instead.
verified_findings.required_design: longitudinal (1-year transition window in P-1348; annual PPMI follow-up; up to 16 years in SNAC-K)
verified_findings.required_modality_family: C3 Molecular/Fluid (CSF p-tau/A-beta and t-tau/A-beta ratios, alpha-synuclein; serum NfL/GFAP) with C5 Clinical/Population biochemistry (Na, TSH, WBC)

evidence_quotes.quote: PD-MCI non-reverters had significantly greater p-tau/A-beta and t-tau/A-beta ratios than reverters across occasions; reverters did not differ from CN on any CSF marker including alpha-synuclein
elevated NfL and GFAP reduced MCI reversion to NC; no biomarker predicted NC-to-MCI development
higher Na (OR 7.3) and lower TSH (OR 3.6) predicted MCI reversion; family history of dementia associated with reversion.

verifier_issues_not_carried_operator_rev: P-1398 CONTAINS AN INTERNAL COUNTEREXAMPLE. In PD-MCI the disease-defining neurodegenerative marker is alpha-synuclein, and the block states there were 'no group differences in p-tau/tau or asyn' for reverters vs CN, with asyn null across groups. So PD neurodegenerative burden did NOT grade reversion in that cohort; only AD co-pathology did. The block's own limitation adds that CSF markers were 'limited to amyloid/tau/asyn without imaging, genetic or cholinergic markers', so 'indistinguishable ... on every CSF marker' is true only of a three-analyte panel.

THE RECORD'S OWN QUOTE CONTRADICTS HALF (b). The P-1348 quote ends 'family history of dementia associated with reversion.' Family history of dementia is an AD/neurodegenerative risk factor, not a treatable metabolic-endocrine one, and it associates POSITIVELY with reversion. The claim that 'the factors that positively predict it are NON-neurodegenerative and largely treatable' is falsified by the evidence the record itself cites and then drops from the statement.

'NEURODEGENERATION-LINKED VARIABLES (age, depressive mood, disease count, low WBC)' IS AN UNSUPPORTED RELABEL. P-1348's block frames exactly these as modifiable: 'Treatable conditions - hypertension, osteoarticular disease, depression, disease accumulation, electrolyte/thyroid imbalances - are associated with short-term cognitive transitions, offering modifiable intervention targets.' Nothing in the block links low WBC or disease count to neurodegeneration. The treatable/neurodegenerative dichotomy is imposed by the record, not found in the paper.

CORPUS CONTRADICTION ON THE SAME TRANSITION, SAME VARIABLE. P-932 (Lothian Birth Cohort 1936, summaries.md line 141505 - and itself a VF-33 supporter) reports: 'A one-unit increase in depressive symptoms significantly increased the likelihood of reverting from MCI to healthy cognition (OR 1.37, 1.05-1.80, p<0.05).' That is the exact opposite sign to the record's assignment of depressive mood to the progression side. Age is also inconsistent across the corpus: P-986 lists 'older age' among factors raising reversion likelihood, P-932 has older age reducing reversion (OR 0.24), P-1348 puts age on the dementia side. A verified finding should not assert a clean dichotomy the corpus already reverses.

DEDUPE MISSED AN EXISTING CORPUS PAPER AND AN OPEN GAP. P-154 (summaries.md line 5733; Tang et al., Heliyon 2024, ADNI, 179 MCI = 47 reverters vs 132 converters, CSF A-beta and tau at baseline and 2-year follow-up, 'significant differences were observed in ApoE, cognitive function scores, brain tissue volume, and CSF biomarker levels') does precisely the amyloid/tau adjudication of reverters that half (a) claims. It also falsifies the still-open candidate gap CLAUDE-ACTOR-G-079, 'No reversion study adjudicates reverters against amyloid/tau biomarkers' (anchors P-986, P-974), which the dedupe_check does not mention. Caveat: the P-154 block is a legacy raw-extract-spillover block (title is a filename, most fields are abstract text), so it needs repair before use as a supporter.

verified_findings.statement: At the MCI stage the translational and mitochondrial-energetic housekeeping machinery is DOWN-regulated, and this is stage-specific rather than a general disease signal. In the NCGG Japanese biobank (1,227 whole-blood RNA-seq samples) the CN-to-MCI transition is down-dominated (590 of 883 DEGs down) and every one of its 8 representative genes is ribosomal (RPL/RPS, qPCR-confirmed), whereas the MCI-to-AD transition is immune / cell-cycle / protein-processing with NO gene overlap between the two stages; in an independent blood-array cohort the six MCI hub genes - TOMM7, COX7C, UQCRQ (mitochondrial OXPHOS), RPL31, RPS24 (ribosomal) and SNRPG (spliceosomal) - are ALL down-regulated in MCI with single-gene AUCs 0.737-0.784; and in laser-captured layer-III frontal pyramidal neurons the mitochondrial-dysfunction pathway is down-regulated at the prodromal (MCI) stage and flips to up-regulated at later stages.

_g4_decisions.detail: Agent 4 appended P-702, P-706 and P-707 to BOTH VF-25 and VF-27. All six appends rejected and reverted to the canonical membership (VF-25 = 12, VF-27 = 10). This is the fourth consecutive batch in which Agent 4 has appended the same batch papers to these two records regardless of domain relevance.

Agent 4 appended P-709 to BOTH VF-25 and VF-27. Both rejected and reverted to canonical membership (VF-25 = 12, VF-27 = 10). FIFTH consecutive batch of this failure (PAPERINGO-c5y). VF-27 grounds: P-709 is a Four Square Step Test psychometrics study; the word 'depression' occurs exactly once in its whole PDF extract, it administers no depression instrument, reports no severity score, no correlation with any brain measure and no conversion outcome, so it cannot bear on a claim about depression SEVERITY being dissociated from MCI neurobiology. VF-25 grounds: VF-25 requires a within-study head-to-head in which a loaded measure separates MCI from its comparator where an unloaded measure does not. P-709 cannot supply one - the extract states 'Healthy controls were only tested with the FSST once', with TUG, BBS, FRT and OLST administered to the MCI group only. The single measure compared between groups (FSST, 15.31 vs 10.55 s, p<0.001) DID separate them, so there is no dissociation and no unloaded counterpart to contrast.

_g4_decisions.detail: Agent 4 (corpus-wide legacy run) appended 74 supporting papers across VF-03, VF-25 and VF-27 - every one of the run reported 74 consensus updates. All 74 reverted to canonical membership (VF-03=5, VF-25=12, VF-27=10). SIXTH consecutive batch of the VF-25/VF-27 failure (PAPERINGO-c5y) and a recurrence of the VF-03 pattern. Grounds: each of these three findings asserts a WITHIN-STUDY head-to-head, and the appends are contiguous blocks of recent paper IDs (P-676..P-753 for VF-25), which is the signature of a mechanical modality/keyword sweep rather than evidence. VF-03 requires a direct longitudinal-versus-cross-sectional comparison: P-578 (amyloid+FDG PET conversion), P-582 (allostatic load), P-746 (semantic networks) are longitudinal but make no such comparison. VF-25 requires a loaded measure to separate MCI where the matched unloaded measure does not, documented per member: P-676, P-723, P-753 and the other 26 report no such dissociation. VF-27 requires depression SEVERITY to be dissociated from neurobiology: P-768 contains no depression measure at all, P-774 has all HAMD-17 below 7 by design with no severity-brain analysis, and P-765 (fractalkine) and P-761 (gait) are unrelated. ONE BORDERLINE RECORDED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED: P-770 does report that the five most frequent NPS including depression showed no significant correlation with orbitofrontal or posterior cingulate volume, which is adjacent to VF-27 - but it scores symptom PRESENCE via NPI domains rather than severity, and the result is published as data not shown, so it is not the documented within-study dissociation every VF-27 member carries. Left out of the membership and raised for manual curation instead.
